section_1.title: Introduction: Functions as Space Mappers
section_1.content: Reframe the function f(x) not as a static graph, but as a transformation of space. Introduce the prerequisite: a function maps points from an 'Input Number Line' to an 'Output Number Line'. Visualize two parallel lines with arrows connecting x to f(x).
section_1.example: Imagine a conveyor belt (Input) and a second belt (Output). The function f(x) = 2x simply takes every point on the first belt and places it twice as far along the second belt.

section_2.title: The Core Concept: Local Scaling Factor
section_2.content: Define the derivative not as the 'slope' of a tangent, but as the 'local scaling factor'. When we move a tiny distance 'dx' on the input line, the output moves 'dy'. The derivative is the ratio of these lengths: how much the space is stretched or squashed at that specific point.
section_2.example: If f'(x) = 3 at a specific point, it means a tiny 1mm segment on the input line is stretched into a 3mm segment on the output line.

section_3.title: The Elastic Ant: Visualizing f(x) = x²
section_3.content: Apply the transformational view to a non-linear function. Use animation to show how the 'stretching' varies. As we move further from zero, the output line stretches more and more. Zoom in on a small neighborhood to show that, locally, every smooth transformation looks like a simple uniform stretch.
section_3.example: An 'Elastic Ant' walks along the input line. When it stands at x=3 (where the derivative of x² is 6), the ground beneath it on the output line is being stretched 6 times wider than its original step.

section_4.title: The Direction of Transformation
section_4.content: Explain the significance of the sign of the derivative in a transformational context. A positive derivative preserves the orientation (forward stays forward), while a negative derivative flips the space (forward becomes backward).
section_4.example: If f(x) = -2x, the output line isn't just stretched; it's flipped horizontally. The ant walking right on the input line sees its shadow moving left on the output line.

section_5.title: Density and Compression
section_5.content: Introduce the concept of 'Point Density'. Where the derivative is high, points are spread out (dilated). Where the derivative is near zero, points are crowded together (compressed). This leads to the idea of critical points being 'singularities' where the transformation momentarily collapses space.
section_5.example: At x=0 for f(x)=x³, the derivative is 0. This 'crushes' a whole neighborhood of input points into a single dense cluster on the output line before they start stretching out again.

section_6.title: Conclusion: Preparing for Higher Dimensions
section_6.content: Summarize the view: Derivative = Local Expansion/Contraction factor. Briefly mention that this perspective is essential for understanding the 'Jacobian' in multivariable calculus, where derivatives describe how areas or volumes are transformed.
section_6.example: Just as a 1D derivative scales a line segment, the Jacobian will later show how a 2D function stretches a square into a distorted parallelogram.

section_4.example: If f(x) = -2x, the output line isn't just stretched; it's flipped horizontally. The ant walking right on the input line sees its shadow moving left on the output line.

section_5.title: Density and Compression
section_5.content: Introduce the concept of 'Point Density'. Where the derivative is high, points are spread out (dilated). Where the derivative is near zero, points are crowded together (compressed). This leads to the idea of critical points being 'singularities' where the transformation momentarily collapses space.
section_5.example: At x=0 for f(x)=x³, the derivative is 0. This 'crushes' a whole neighborhood of input points into a single dense cluster on the output line before they start stretching out again.

section_6.title: Conclusion: Preparing for Higher Dimensions
section_6.content: Summarize the view: Derivative = Local Expansion/Contraction factor. Briefly mention that this perspective is essential for understanding the 'Jacobian' in multivariable calculus, where derivatives describe how areas or volumes are transformed.
section_6.example: Just as a 1D derivative scales a line segment, the Jacobian will later show how a 2D function stretches a square into a distorted parallelogram.

section_1.title: Introduction: Functions as Space Mappers
lecture_lines: Think of functions as mapping one space to another.
Input points move to new positions on the output.
For f(x) equals 2x, every point moves twice as far.
animations: Display the title 'Functions as Space Mappers' in #FFFFFF at the top.
Draw two parallel horizontal lines: Input line at y=1 and Output line at y=-1 in #888888.
Highlight a point 'x' on the Input line at x=1 in #00FF00.
Draw an arrow from Input 'x' to Output '2x' at x=2 in #00FFFF to show mapping.
Show multiple arrows mapping points [0, 0.5, 1] to [0, 1, 2] to visualize stretching.

section_2.title: The Core Concept: Local Scaling Factor
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure the local scaling factor of space.
Imagine a tiny segment dx on the input line.
This segment transforms into a new length dy.
The derivative is the ratio of these local lengths.
It tells us how much space stretches or squashes.
animations: Display the text 'Local Scaling Factor' in #FFFFFF.
On the Input line, highlight a tiny segment 'dx' in #FF00FF.
On the Output line, show the corresponding segment 'dy' in #FFFF00.
Animate 'dy' stretching to be three times longer than 'dx'.
Display the formula f'(x) = dy / dx in #00FFFF near the segments.

section_3.title: The Elastic Ant: Visualizing f(x) = x²
lecture_lines: For non-linear functions, the scaling varies at every point.
Imagine an ant walking along the input number line.
At x equals three, the ground stretches six times wider.
Zooming in, the transformation looks like a uniform stretch.
The derivative captures this local, linear expansion factor.
animations: Display the function f(x) = x^2 in #FFFFFF.
A small circle (the ant) moves along the Input line from x=2 to x=3.
Highlight a 0.2-unit segment around the ant at x=3 in #FF0000.
Show the corresponding 1.2-unit segment on the Output line in #00FF00.
Zoom into the neighborhood of x=3 until the stretching looks linear.

section_4.title: The Direction of Transformation
lecture_lines: The sign of the derivative determines the mapping's direction.
A positive derivative preserves the original orientation of space.
A negative derivative flips the space in the output.
animations: Display the text 'Direction of Transformation' in #FFFFFF.
Show an arrow moving right on the Input line.
For f(x) = 2x, show an arrow moving right on the Output line in #00FF00.
Change the function to f(x) = -2x and show the Output arrow flipping left.
Highlight the reversal of orientation with a brief flash in #FF0000.

section_5.title: Density and Compression
lecture_lines: Derivatives also reveal how point density changes during mapping.
High derivatives spread points out, creating lower density.
Low derivatives crowd points together, increasing the local density.
At critical points, the derivative is zero, collapsing space.
This 'crushing' effect happens momentarily before space expands again.
animations: Place 10 dots uniformly on the Input line between -1 and 1.
Map these dots to the Output line using the function f(x) = x^3.
Show the dots clustering tightly near the origin on the Output line.
Highlight the high-density cluster at x=0 with a glow effect in #FFFF00.
Contrast this with the sparse distribution of dots far from the origin.

section_6.title: Conclusion: Preparing for Higher Dimensions
lecture_lines: The derivative is a local expansion or contraction factor.
This view extends to higher dimensions via the Jacobian.
Higher-order derivatives describe complex transformations of areas and volumes.
animations: Fade out the parallel lines and display 'Derivative = Local Scaling' in #FFFFFF.
Morph the number lines into a 2D coordinate grid in #333333.
Highlight a small unit square in the Input space in #00FFFF.
Transform the square into a distorted parallelogram in the Output space in #FF00FF.
Display the label 'Jacobian' in #FFFFFF next to the transformation.

outline.title: Density and Compression
outline.content: Introduce the concept of 'Point Density'. Where the derivative is high, points are spread out (dilated). Where the derivative is near zero, points are crowded together (compressed). This leads to the idea of critical points being 'singularities' where the transformation momentarily collapses space.
outline.example: At x=0 for f(x)=x³, the derivative is 0. This 'crushes' a whole neighborhood of input points into a single dense cluster on the output line before they start stretching out again.

storyboard.title: Density and Compression
lecture_lines: Derivatives also reveal how point density changes during mapping.
High derivatives spread points out, creating lower density.
Low derivatives crowd points together, increasing the local density.
At critical points, the derivative is zero, collapsing space.
This 'crushing' effect happens momentarily before space expands again.
animations: Place 10 dots uniformly on the Input line between -1 and 1.
Map these dots to the Output line using the function f(x) = x^3.
Show the dots clustering tightly near the origin on the Output line.
Highlight the high-density cluster at x=0 with a glow effect in #FFFF00.
Contrast this with the sparse distribution of dots far from the origin.

outline.title: The Direction of Transformation
outline.content: Explain the significance of the sign of the derivative in a transformational context. A positive derivative preserves the orientation (forward stays forward), while a negative derivative flips the space (forward becomes backward).
outline.example: If f(x) = -2x, the output line isn't just stretched; it's flipped horizontally. The ant walking right on the input line sees its shadow moving left on the output line.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initializing the layout with the specific title and lecture lines for Section 1
        self.setup_layout(
            "Functions as Space Mappers", 
            [
                "Think of functions as mapping one space to another.",
                "Input points move to new positions on the output.",
                "For f(x) equals 2x, every point moves twice as far."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Reframe the function f(x) not as a static graph, but as a transformation of space.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Drawing two parallel horizontal lines: Input at Row B (y=1.2) and Output at Row E (y=-1.8)
        # Using columns 1 to 6 to span the right-side visual area.
        input_line = Line(start=self.grid["B1"], end=self.grid["B6"], color="#888888")
        output_line = Line(start=self.grid["E1"], end=self.grid["E6"], color="#888888")
        
        input_label = Text("Input", font_size=18, color="#888888")
        output_label = Text("Output", font_size=18, color="#888888")
        
        # Place labels to the right of the lines (Column 6) to avoid interference with arrows
        self.place_at_grid(input_label, "B6", scale_factor=0.8).shift(RIGHT * 0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(output_label, "E6", scale_factor=0.8).shift(RIGHT * 0.5)

        self.play(Create(input_line), Create(output_line), FadeIn(input_label), FadeIn(output_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight a point 'x' on the Input line at x=1 (placed at Grid B3)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        point_x = Dot(point=self.grid["B3"], color="#00FF00")
        label_x = MathTex("x", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        # Position label_x above the point (Grid A3) - B001/B009 compliant
        self.place_at_grid(label_x, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Draw an initial arrow showing mapping from Input 'x' (B3) to Output '2x'
        # In f(x)=2x, if B3 is math x=1, the output 2x=2 corresponds to Grid E4 (math x=2).
        mapping_arrow = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["B3"], 
            end=self.grid["E4"], 
            buff=0.1, 
            color="#00FFFF", 
            stroke_width=3
        )
        point_fx = Dot(point=self.grid["E4"], color="#00FFFF")
        label_fx = MathTex("f(x)", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        # Position label_fx below the point (Grid F4)
        self.place_at_grid(label_fx, "F4", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(FadeIn(point_x), Write(label_x))
        self.play(GrowArrow(mapping_arrow), FadeIn(point_fx), Write(label_fx))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # For f(x)=2x, every point moves twice as far. Show multiple arrows mapping points [0, 0.5, 1] to [0, 1, 2].
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # Define points and their maps
        # Math x=0 -> Grid B2, Math x=0.5 -> (B2+B3)/2, Math x=1 -> Grid B3
        # Math y=0 -> Grid E2, Math y=1 -> Grid E3, Math y=2 -> Grid E4
        
        points_input = [
            self.grid["B2"], 
            (self.grid["B2"] + self.grid["B3"]) / 2, 
            self.grid["B3"]
        ]
        points_output = [
            self.grid["E2"], 
            self.grid["E3"], 
            self.grid["E4"]
        ]
        
        arrows = VGroup(*[
            Arrow(start=pi, end=po, buff=0.1, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2) 
            for pi, po in zip(points_input, points_output)
        ])
        
        # We already have mapping_arrow and point_fx for x=1. Let's just animate the group.
        # Remove the previous single arrow/dot to avoid duplication when showing the group
        self.remove(mapping_arrow, point_fx)
        
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in arrows], lag_ratio=0.3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Preparing for Higher Dimensions", [
            "The derivative is a local expansion or contraction factor.",
            "This view extends to higher dimensions via the Jacobian.",
            "Higher-order derivatives describe complex transformations of areas and volumes."
        ])
        
        # Initial visual setup: 1D parallel lines from previous context
        line_input = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B6"], color="#555555")
        line_output = Line(self.grid["D2"], self.grid["D6"], color="#555555")
        self.add(line_input, line_output)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Display 'Derivative = Local Scaling'
        scaling_text = MathTex(r"\text{Derivative} = \text{Local Scaling}", color="#FFFFFF")
        # Apply B002: Use area for horizontally extended text
        self.place_in_area(scaling_text, "A2", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(scaling_text, shift=UP),
            line_input.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.5),
            line_output.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Morph the number lines into a 2D coordinate grid in #333333
        grid_2d = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#333333", "stroke_width": 2, "stroke_opacity": 0.6},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": "#333333", "stroke_width": 2}

        # Apply B021 and positioning constraints: place grid in the center-right visual area
        self.place_in_area(grid_2d, "B2", "F6")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(scaling_text),
            ReplacementTransform(VGroup(line_input, line_output), grid_2d),
            run_time=2
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        square = Square(side_length=1.0, stroke_color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color="#00FFFF")

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)

            "The derivative is the ratio of these local lengths.",

        self.play(Create(dy_segment), FadeIn(dy_label))

            Write(formula),

        )

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Initial Setup
        title_text = "The Direction of Transformation"

            "- A positive derivative preserves the original orientation of space.",
            "- A negative derivative flips the space in the output."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_INPUT = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_POSITIVE = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_NEGATIVE = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The sign of the derivative determines the mapping's direction."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_INPUT)

        # Input and Output Lines

        input_line = NumberLine(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], length=3.5, include_numbers=True, font_size=18, color=COLOR_INPUT)
        output_line = NumberLine(x_range=[-6, 6, 2], length=3.5, include_numbers=True, font_size=18, color=COLOR_INPUT)

        self.place_in_area(output_line, 'E3', 'E6')
        
        input_label = Text("Input", font_size=20, color=COLOR_INPUT)
        output_label = Text("Output", font_size=20, color=COLOR_INPUT)
        
        # Position labels offset from the movement area (B013)
        self.place_at_grid(input_label, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(output_label, 'E2', scale_factor=0.8)

        # Initial function display
        func_label = MathTex("f(x) = 2x", font_size=36, color=COLOR_POSITIVE)
        self.place_in_area(func_label, 'C3', 'C6')

        self.play(
            Create(input_line),
            Create(output_line),
            Write(input_label),
            Write(output_label),
            Write(func_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "A positive derivative preserves the original orientation of space."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_POSITIVE)

        # ValueTracker for smooth movement
        t = ValueTracker(0)

        # Create arrows that will be updated by the ValueTracker
        input_arrow = Arrow(color=COLOR_INPUT, stroke_width=4, buff=0)
        output_arrow = Arrow(color=COLOR_POSITIVE, stroke_width=4, buff=0)

        def update_input_arrow(mob):
            val = t.get_value()
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(input_line.n2p(val), input_line.n2p(val + 0.5))

        def update_output_arrow_pos(mob):
            val = t.get_value()
            # f(x) = 2x mapping
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(output_line.n2p(2 * val), output_line.n2p(2 * (val + 0.5)))

        input_arrow.add_updater(update_input_arrow)
        output_arrow.add_updater(update_output_arrow_pos)

        self.add(input_arrow, output_arrow)
        # Animate from 0 to 1 on the input line
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(1), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "A negative derivative flips the space in the output."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_NEGATIVE)

        # Transition to f(x) = -2x
        new_func_label = MathTex("f(x) = -2x", font_size=36, color=COLOR_NEGATIVE)
        self.place_in_area(new_func_label, 'C3', 'C6')

        # Reset ValueTracker and update the output arrow behavior
        self.play(
            FadeOut(input_arrow),
            FadeOut(output_arrow),
            Transform(func_label, new_func_label),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        t.set_value(0)
        output_arrow.remove_updater(update_output_arrow_pos)
        output_arrow.set_color(COLOR_NEGATIVE)

        def update_output_arrow_neg(mob):
            val = t.get_value()
            # f(x) = -2x mapping
            # Input forward: [val, val+0.5] -> Output: [-2*val, -2*(val+0.5)]
            # Since -2*(val+0.5) < -2*val, the arrow points left (reversal)
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(output_line.n2p(-2 * val), output_line.n2p(-2 * (val + 0.5)))

        # Highlight reversal of orientation with a brief flash (FF0000)
        flash = Flash(output_line.n2p(0), color=COLOR_NEGATIVE, flash_radius=0.5)
        
        self.play(flash)
        
        input_arrow.add_updater(update_input_arrow)
        output_arrow.add_updater(update_output_arrow_neg)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(input_arrow),
            FadeIn(output_arrow)
        )
        
        # Animate movement showing the flipped direction
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(1), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

        # Final cleanup
        input_arrow.remove_updater(update_input_arrow)
        output_arrow.remove_updater(update_output_arrow_neg)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "Density and Compression"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Derivatives also reveal how point density changes during mapping.",
            "High derivatives spread points out, creating lower density.",
            "Low derivatives crowd points together, increasing the local density.",
            "At critical points, the derivative is zero, collapsing space.",
            "This 'crushing' effect happens momentarily before space expands again."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        C_INTRO = "#88C0D0" # Frost Blue
        C_SPREAD = "#A3BE8C" # Green
        C_CROWD = "#EBCB8B" # Yellow-ish
        C_CRUSH = "#FFFF00" # Pure Yellow (as per Issue 23)
        C_EXPAND = "#D08770" # Orange

        # 1. Setup Static Visuals (Number Lines and Labels)
        # Using grey for background infrastructure
        input_line = NumberLine(
            x_range=[-1.2, 1.2, 0.5], 
            length=4, 
            include_numbers=True, 
            font_size=18, 
            color=GRAY_C
        )
        output_line = NumberLine(
            x_range=[-1.2, 1.2, 0.5], 
            length=4, 
            include_numbers=True, 
            font_size=18, 
            color=GRAY_C
        )
        
        # Positions (B2-B5 and E2-E5)
        # B021: Visual area starts at Col 2 to maintain gap from lecture
        self.place_in_area(input_line, "B2", "B5")
        self.place_in_area(output_line, "E2", "E5")
        
        # Labels (A2 and D2)
        # B001/B013: Labels offset from the action area and non-overlapping
        input_label = Text("Input x", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        output_label = Text("Output f(x) = x³", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(input_label, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(output_label, "D2")
        
        self.add(input_line, output_line, input_label, output_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Derivatives reveal point density changes.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(C_INTRO))
        
        # 10 dots uniformly on the Input line between -1 and 1.
        x_vals = np.linspace(-1, 1, 10)
        input_dots = VGroup(*[
            Dot(input_line.n2p(x), radius=0.08, color=C_INTRO) 
            for x in x_vals
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(input_dots))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # High derivatives spread points out.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(C_SPREAD))
        
        # Mapping dots: x -> x^3
        output_dots = VGroup(*[
            Dot(output_line.n2p(x**3), radius=0.08, color=C_SPREAD) 
            for x in x_vals
        ])
        
        # We'll use a copy of input dots to animate the mapping (B009: vertical path is clear)
        mapping_dots = input_dots.copy()
        self.play(Transform(mapping_dots, output_dots), run_time=2)
        self.add(output_dots)
        self.remove(mapping_dots)
        
        # Show stretching highlights (outer dots)
        outer_rects = VGroup(
            SurroundingRectangle(output_dots[0:2], color=C_SPREAD, buff=0.1),
            SurroundingRectangle(output_dots[8:10], color=C_SPREAD, buff=0.1)
        )
        self.play(Create(outer_rects))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(outer_rects))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Low derivatives crowd points together.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(C_CROWD))
        
        # Highlight clustering near origin
        self.play(output_dots[3:7].animate.set_color(C_CROWD))
        inner_rect = SurroundingRectangle(output_dots[4:6], color=C_CROWD, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(inner_rect))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(inner_rect))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Critical points (f'(0)=0) collapse space.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(C_CRUSH))
        
        # High-density glow effect at x=0
        glow = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=r, color=C_CRUSH, fill_opacity=op, stroke_width=0)
            for r, op in zip([0.15, 0.25, 0.35], [0.6, 0.3, 0.1])
        ])
        glow.move_to(output_line.n2p(0))
        
        # Derivative label - B001/B013: placed at D5 to avoid clustering in center
        deriv_label = MathTex("f'(0) = 0", font_size=24, color=C_CRUSH)
        self.place_at_grid(deriv_label, "D5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(glow, scale=0.2), Write(deriv_label))
        self.play(glow.animate.scale(1.5), run_time=1, rate_func=there_and_back)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Crushing happens momentarily before expansion.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(C_EXPAND))
        
        # Arrows showing expansion
        arrow_l = Arrow(output_line.n2p(-0.2), output_line.n2p(-0.9), color=C_EXPAND, buff=0, tip_length=0.15)
        arrow_r = Arrow(output_line.n2p(0.2), output_line.n2p(0.9), color=C_EXPAND, buff=0, tip_length=0.15)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_l), GrowArrow(arrow_r))
        # Final pulse to emphasize the singularity
        self.play(glow.animate.scale(0.8), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(glow.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=0.5)
        
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: Introduction: Functions as Space Mappers
section_1.content: Reframe the function f(x) not as a static graph, but as a transformation of space. Introduce the prerequisite: a function maps points from an 'Input Number Line' to an 'Output Number Line'. Visualize two parallel lines with arrows connecting x to f(x).
section_1.example: Imagine a conveyor belt (Input) and a second belt (Output). The function f(x) = 2x simply takes every point on the first belt and places it twice as far along the second belt.

section_2.title: The Core Concept: Local Scaling Factor
section_2.content: Define the derivative not as the 'slope' of a tangent, but as the 'local scaling factor'. When we move a tiny distance 'dx' on the input line, the output moves 'dy'. The derivative is the ratio of these lengths: how much the space is stretched or squashed at that specific point.
section_2.example: If f'(x) = 3 at a specific point, it means a tiny 1mm segment on the input line is stretched into a 3mm segment on the output line.

section_3.title: The Elastic Ant: Visualizing f(x) = x²
section_3.content: Apply the transformational view to a non-linear function. Use animation to show how the 'stretching' varies. As we move further from zero, the output line stretches more and more. Zoom in on a small neighborhood to show that, locally, every smooth transformation looks like a simple uniform stretch.
section_3.example: An 'Elastic Ant' walks along the input line. When it stands at x=3 (where the derivative of x² is 6), the ground beneath it on the output line is being stretched 6 times wider than its original step.

section_4.title: The Direction of Transformation
section_4.content: Explain the significance of the sign of the derivative in a transformational context. A positive derivative preserves the orientation (forward stays forward), while a negative derivative flips the space (forward becomes backward).
section_4.example: If f(x) = -2x, the output line isn't just stretched; it's flipped horizontally. The ant walking right on the input line sees its shadow moving left on the output line.

section_5.title: Density and Compression
section_5.content: Introduce the concept of 'Point Density'. Where the derivative is high, points are spread out (dilated). Where the derivative is near zero, points are crowded together (compressed). This leads to the idea of critical points being 'singularities' where the transformation momentarily collapses space.
section_5.example: At x=0 for f(x)=x³, the derivative is 0. This 'crushes' a whole neighborhood of input points into a single dense cluster on the output line before they start stretching out again.

section_6.title: Conclusion: Preparing for Higher Dimensions
section_6.content: Summarize the view: Derivative = Local Expansion/Contraction factor. Briefly mention that this perspective is essential for understanding the 'Jacobian' in multivariable calculus, where derivatives describe how areas or volumes are transformed.
section_6.example: Just as a 1D derivative scales a line segment, the Jacobian will later show how a 2D function stretches a square into a distorted parallelogram.

            self.grid["E3"], 
            self.grid["E4"]
        ]

        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in arrows], lag_ratio=0.3),
            run_time=2
        )

        lecture_lines = [
            "- Derivatives measure the local scaling factor of space.",

            "- It tells us how much space stretches or squashes."
        ]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_text))
        scaling_text = Text("Local Scaling Factor", font_size=32, color=color_text)

        self.play(Write(scaling_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        dx_start_num = 1.0

            input_line.number_to_point(dx_start_num + dx_val),
            color=color_dx, stroke_width=10
        )
        dx_label = MathTex("dx", color=color_dx, font_size=30)
        dx_label.next_to(dx_segment, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(input_line), FadeIn(input_label))
        self.play(Create(dx_segment), FadeIn(dx_label))

            output_line.number_to_point(dy_start_num + dy_length_initial),

        self.play(Create(dy_segment), FadeIn(dy_label))
        self.wait(1)

        stretch_tracker = ValueTracker(dy_length_initial)
        
        dy_segment.add_updater(
            lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners([
                output_line.number_to_point(dy_start_num),
                output_line.number_to_point(dy_start_num + stretch_tracker.get_value())
            ])
        )
        dy_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dy_segment, DOWN, buff=0.1))
        
        formula = MathTex(
            "f'(x) = \\frac{dy}{dx} = \\frac{1.5}{0.5} = 3", 
            color=color_formula, font_size=36
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, "D1", "D6")
        
        self.play(
            stretch_tracker.animate.set_value(dy_length_final),
            Write(formula),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        dy_segment.clear_updaters()
        dy_label.clear_updaters()

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(color_text))
        
        highlight_box = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=color_formula, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(highlight_box))
        self.play(Indicate(dy_segment, color=color_dy, scale_factor=1.2))
        self.play(FadeOut(highlight_box))
        
        self.wait(3)

            "- A positive derivative preserves the original orientation of space.",
            "- A negative derivative flips the space in the output."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_INPUT = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_POSITIVE = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_NEGATIVE = "#FF0000"

        input_arrow = Arrow(color=COLOR_INPUT, stroke_width=4, buff=0)
        output_arrow = Arrow(color=COLOR_POSITIVE, stroke_width=4, buff=0)

        def update_input_arrow(mob):
            val = t.get_value()
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(input_line.n2p(val), input_line.n2p(val + 0.5))

        def update_output_arrow_pos(mob):

        self.play(
            FadeOut(input_arrow),
            FadeOut(output_arrow),
            Transform(func_label, new_func_label),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        t.set_value(0)
        output_arrow.remove_updater(update_output_arrow_pos)
        output_arrow.set_color(COLOR_NEGATIVE)

        def update_output_arrow_neg(mob):
            val = t.get_value()
            # f(x) = -2x mapping
            # Input forward: [val, val+0.5] -> Output: [-2*val, -2*(val+0.5)]
            # Since -2*(val+0.5) < -2*val, the arrow points left (reversal)
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(output_line.n2p(-2 * val), output_line.n2p(-2 * (val + 0.5)))

        # Highlight reversal of orientation with a brief flash (FF0000)
        flash = Flash(output_line.n2p(0), color=COLOR_NEGATIVE, flash_radius=0.5)
        
        self.play(flash)
        
        input_arrow.add_updater(update_input_arrow)
        output_arrow.add_updater(update_output_arrow_neg)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(input_arrow),
            FadeIn(output_arrow)
        )
        
        # Animate movement showing the flipped direction
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(1), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

        # Final cleanup
        input_arrow.remove_updater(update_input_arrow)
        output_arrow.remove_updater(update_output_arrow_neg)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "Density and Compression"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Derivatives also reveal how point density changes during mapping.",
            "High derivatives spread points out, creating lower density.",
            "Low derivatives crowd points together, increasing the local density.",
            "At critical points, the derivative is zero, collapsing space.",
            "This 'crushing' effect happens momentarily before space expands again."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        C_INTRO = "#88C0D0" # Frost Blue
        C_SPREAD = "#A3BE8C" # Green
        C_CROWD = "#EBCB8B" # Yellow-ish
        C_CRUSH = "#FFFF00" # Pure Yellow (as per Issue 23)
        C_EXPAND = "#D08770" # Orange

        # 1. Setup Static Visuals (Number Lines and Labels)
        # Using label_constructor=Text to bypass LaTeX dependency
        input_line = NumberLine(
            x_range=[-1.2, 1.2, 0.5], 
            length=4, 
            include_numbers=True, 
            font_size=18, 
            color=GRAY_C,
            label_constructor=Text
        )
        output_line = NumberLine(
            x_range=[-1.2, 1.2, 0.5], 
            length=4, 
            include_numbers=True, 
            font_size=18, 
            color=GRAY_C,
            label_constructor=Text
        )
        
        # Positions (B2-B5 and E2-E5)
        self.place_in_area(input_line, "B2", "B5")
        self.place_in_area(output_line, "E2", "E5")
        
        # Labels (A2 and D2)
        input_label = Text("Input x", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        output_label = Text("Output f(x) = x³", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(input_label, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(output_label, "D2")
        
        self.add(input_line, output_line, input_label, output_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(C_INTRO))
        
        x_vals = np.linspace(-1, 1, 10)
        input_dots = VGroup(*[
            Dot(input_line.n2p(x), radius=0.08, color=C_INTRO) 
            for x in x_vals
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(input_dots))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(C_SPREAD))
        
        output_dots = VGroup(*[
            Dot(output_line.n2p(x**3), radius=0.08, color=C_SPREAD) 
            for x in x_vals
        ])
        
        mapping_dots = input_dots.copy()
        self.play(Transform(mapping_dots, output_dots), run_time=2)
        self.add(output_dots)
        self.remove(mapping_dots)
        
        outer_rects = VGroup(
            SurroundingRectangle(output_dots[0:2], color=C_SPREAD, buff=0.1),
            SurroundingRectangle(output_dots[8:10], color=C_SPREAD, buff=0.1)
        )
        self.play(Create(outer_rects))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(outer_rects))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(C_CROWD))
        
        self.play(output_dots[3:7].animate.set_color(C_CROWD))
        inner_rect = SurroundingRectangle(output_dots[4:6], color=C_CROWD, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(inner_rect))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(inner_rect))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(C_CRUSH))
        
        glow = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=r, color=C_CRUSH, fill_opacity=op, stroke_width=0)
            for r, op in zip([0.15, 0.25, 0.35], [0.6, 0.3, 0.1])
        ])
        glow.move_to(output_line.n2p(0))
        
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to bypass LaTeX dependency
        deriv_label = Text("f'(0) = 0", font_size=24, color=C_CRUSH)
        self.place_at_grid(deriv_label, "D5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(glow, scale=0.2), Write(deriv_label))
        self.play(glow.animate.scale(1.5), run_time=1, rate_func=there_and_back)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(C_EXPAND))
        
        arrow_l = Arrow(output_line.n2p(-0.2), output_line.n2p(-0.9), color=C_EXPAND, buff=0, tip_length=0.15)
        arrow_r = Arrow(output_line.n2p(0.2), output_line.n2p(0.9), color=C_EXPAND, buff=0, tip_length=0.15)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_l), GrowArrow(arrow_r))
        self.play(glow.animate.scale(0.8), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(glow.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=0.5)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Preparing for Higher Dimensions", [
            "The derivative is a local expansion or contraction factor.",
            "This view extends to higher dimensions via the Jacobian.",
            "Higher-order derivatives describe complex transformations of areas and volumes."
        ])
        
        # Initial visual setup: 1D parallel lines from previous context
        line_input = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B6"], color="#555555")
        line_output = Line(self.grid["D2"], self.grid["D6"], color="#555555")
        self.add(line_input, line_output)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Display 'Derivative = Local Scaling'
        scaling_text = MathTex(r"\text{Derivative} = \text{Local Scaling}", color="#FFFFFF")
        # Apply B002: Use area for horizontally extended text
        self.place_in_area(scaling_text, "A2", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(scaling_text, shift=UP),
            line_input.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.5),
            line_output.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Morph the number lines into a 2D coordinate grid in #333333
        grid_2d = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#333333", "stroke_width": 2, "stroke_opacity": 0.6},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": "#333333", "stroke_width": 2}
        )
        # Apply B021 and positioning constraints: place grid in the center-right visual area
        self.place_in_area(grid_2d, "B2", "F6")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(scaling_text),
            ReplacementTransform(VGroup(line_input, line_output), grid_2d),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight a unit square in the Input space in #00FFFF
        # We create it at a fixed size and then use the grid system for consistent placement
        square = Square(side_length=1.0, stroke_color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color="#00FFFF")
        # Center it relative to the visual area (D4 is roughly center of B2-F6)
        self.place_at_grid(square, "D4")
        
        # Define the transformed parallelogram in #FF00FF
        # This represents the output of a 2D linear transformation (Jacobian)
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            [-0.5, -0.5, 0], [1.0, 0, 0], [1.3, 1.2, 0], [-0.2, 0.7, 0],
            stroke_color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color="#FF00FF"
        )
        self.place_at_grid(parallelogram, "D4")
        
        # Jacobian label
        jacobian_label = Text("Jacobian", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        # Apply B038: Position away from center/axes to avoid congestion
        self.place_at_grid(jacobian_label, "B5") 

        self.play(Create(square))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(square, parallelogram),
            Write(jacobian_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Final cleanup
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "For non-linear functions, the scaling varies at every point.",
            "Imagine an ant walking along the input number line.",
            "At x equals three, the ground stretches six times wider.",
            "Zooming in, the transformation looks like a uniform stretch.",
            "The derivative captures this local, linear expansion factor."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Elastic Ant: Visualizing f(x) = x²", lecture_lines)

        # Colors for matching lecture lines
        COLOR_FUNC = "#FFFFFF" # White
        COLOR_ANT = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        COLOR_INPUT = "#FF0000" # Red
        COLOR_OUTPUT = "#00FF00" # Green
        COLOR_ZOOM = "#00FFFF"  # Cyan
        COLOR_DERIV = "#FFC0CB" # Pink

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "For non-linear functions, the scaling varies at every point."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_FUNC))
        
        func_text = MathTex("f(x) = x^2", color=COLOR_FUNC)
        # B002: Using place_in_area for extended mobject
        self.place_in_area(func_text, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        input_line = NumberLine(x_range=[0, 4, 1], length=5, include_numbers=True, font_size=16)
        output_line = NumberLine(x_range=[0, 10, 2], length=5, include_numbers=True, font_size=16)
        
        self.place_in_area(input_line, "B1", "B6")
        self.place_in_area(output_line, "E1", "E6")
        
        input_label = Text("Input (x)", font_size=16, color=BLUE_B)
        output_label = Text("Output (f(x))", font_size=16, color=GREEN_B)
        
        # Position labels offset from lines
        self.place_at_grid(input_label, "B1", scale_factor=0.8).shift(LEFT * 0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(output_label, "E1", scale_factor=0.8).shift(LEFT * 0.8)

        self.play(
            Write(func_text),
            Create(input_line),
            Create(output_line),
            Write(input_label),
            Write(output_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Imagine an ant walking along the input number line."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_ANT)
        )
        
        ant = Circle(radius=0.1, color=COLOR_ANT, fill_opacity=0.8)
        # Position at x=2 initially
        ant.move_to(input_line.n2p(2))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(ant))
        # Ant walks to x=3. B009: Path is clear of labels (which are in rows A, C, E).
        self.play(ant.animate.move_to(input_line.n2p(3)), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "At x equals three, the ground stretches six times wider."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_INPUT)
        )
        
        # Highlight segment on input line around x=3 (0.2 units: 2.9 to 3.1)
        input_segment = Line(input_line.n2p(2.9), input_line.n2p(3.1), color=COLOR_INPUT, stroke_width=8)
        
        # Highlight segment on output line around f(3)=9
        # f(2.9)=8.41, f(3.1)=9.61. Length = 1.2 (which is 6 * 0.2)
        output_segment = Line(output_line.n2p(8.41), output_line.n2p(9.61), color=COLOR_OUTPUT, stroke_width=8)
        
        stretch_label = MathTex("\\text{Stretch: } 6\\times", color=COLOR_INPUT)
        self.place_at_grid(stretch_label, "C4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Visual mapping connection
        mapping_arrow = Arrow(start=input_line.n2p(3), end=output_line.n2p(9), color=WHITE, stroke_width=2, buff=0.2)

        self.play(
            Create(input_segment),
            Create(output_segment),
            Write(stretch_label),
            GrowArrow(mapping_arrow)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Zooming in, the transformation looks like a uniform stretch."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_ZOOM)
        )
        
        # Zoom effect focused on x=3 and f(3)=9
        zoom_factor = 4
        self.play(
            input_line.animate.scale(zoom_factor, about_point=input_line.n2p(3)),
            output_line.animate.scale(zoom_factor, about_point=output_line.n2p(9)),
            input_segment.animate.scale(zoom_factor, about_point=input_line.n2p(3)),
            output_segment.animate.scale(zoom_factor, about_point=output_line.n2p(9)),
            ant.animate.scale(2, about_point=input_line.n2p(3)),
            FadeOut(stretch_label),
            FadeOut(mapping_arrow),
            FadeOut(input_label),
            FadeOut(output_label),
            FadeOut(func_text)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "The derivative captures this local, linear expansion factor."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_DERIV)
        )
        
        deriv_formula = MathTex("f'(x) = 2x", color=COLOR_DERIV)
        deriv_at_3 = MathTex("f'(3) = 6", color=COLOR_DERIV)
        
        # B001: Ensure coordinates do not overlap. C3 and C5 are separated.
        self.place_at_grid(deriv_formula, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(deriv_at_3, "C5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(deriv_formula))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(deriv_at_3))
        
        self.wait(2)

        self.place_at_grid(label_fx, "F4", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(FadeIn(point_x), Write(label_x))
        self.play(GrowArrow(mapping_arrow), FadeIn(point_fx), Write(label_fx))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # For f(x)=2x, every point moves twice as far. Show multiple arrows mapping points [0, 0.5, 1] to [0, 1, 2].
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # Define points and their maps
        # Math x=0 -> Grid B2, Math x=0.5 -> (B2+B3)/2, Math x=1 -> Grid B3
        # Math y=0 -> Grid E2, Math y=1 -> Grid E3, Math y=2 -> Grid E4
        
        points_input = [
            self.grid["B2"], 
            (self.grid["B2"] + self.grid["B3"]) / 2,

        ]

            self.grid["E2"],

        ]

        )

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        # Initialize layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Preparing for Higher Dimensions", [
            "The derivative is a local expansion or contraction factor.",
            "This view extends to higher dimensions via the Jacobian.",

        ])
        
        # Initial visual setup: 1D parallel lines from previous context
        line_input = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B6"], color="#555555")
        line_output = Line(self.grid["D2"], self.grid["D6"], color="#555555")
        self.add(line_input, line_output)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(scaling_text, shift=UP),
            line_input.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.5),

        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#333333", "stroke_width": 2, "stroke_opacity": 0.6},

            FadeOut(scaling_text),
            ReplacementTransform(VGroup(line_input, line_output), grid_2d),

        )

        )
        self.place_at_grid(parallelogram, "D4")

        # Apply B038: Position away from center/axes to avoid congestion
        self.place_at_grid(jacobian_label, "B5") 

        self.play(Create(square))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(square, parallelogram),
            Write(jacobian_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Final cleanup
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Core Concept: Local Scaling Factor
outline.content: Define the derivative not as the 'slope' of a tangent, but as the 'local scaling factor'. When we move a tiny distance 'dx' on the input line, the output moves 'dy'. The derivative is the ratio of these lengths: how much the space is stretched or squashed at that specific point.
outline.example: If f'(x) = 3 at a specific point, it means a tiny 1mm segment on the input line is stretched into a 3mm segment on the output line.

storyboard.title: The Core Concept: Local Scaling Factor
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure the local scaling factor of space.
Imagine a tiny segment dx on the input line.
This segment transforms into a new length dy.
The derivative is the ratio of these local lengths.
It tells us how much space stretches or squashes.
animations: Display the text 'Local Scaling Factor' in #FFFFFF.
On the Input line, highlight a tiny segment 'dx' in #FF00FF.
On the Output line, show the corresponding segment 'dy' in #FFFF00.
Animate 'dy' stretching to be three times longer than 'dx'.
Display the formula f'(x) = dy / dx in #00FFFF near the segments.

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section 2: The Core Concept: Local Scaling Factor
        title_text = "The Core Concept: Local Scaling Factor"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Derivatives measure the local scaling factor of space.",
            "- Imagine a tiny segment dx on the input line.",
            "- This segment transforms into a new length dy.",

        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        input_line = NumberLine(x_range=[0, 5, 1], length=4.5, include_numbers=True, color=BLUE_B)
        output_line = NumberLine(x_range=[0, 15, 3], length=4.5, include_numbers=True, color=GREEN_B)
        
        input_label = Text("Input", font_size=20, color=BLUE_B)
        output_label = Text("Output", font_size=20, color=GREEN_B)

        self.place_in_area(input_line, "B1", "B6")
        self.place_at_grid(input_label, "B1", scale_factor=0.8).shift(LEFT * 0.8)
        self.place_in_area(output_line, "E1", "E6")
        self.place_at_grid(output_label, "E1", scale_factor=0.8).shift(LEFT * 0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_text))
        scaling_text = Text("Local Scaling Factor", font_size=32, color=color_text)
        self.place_in_area(scaling_text, "A1", "A6")
        self.play(Write(scaling_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_dx))
        
        dx_val = 0.5
        dx_start_num = 1.0

            input_line.number_to_point(dx_start_num),
            input_line.number_to_point(dx_start_num + dx_val),
            color=color_dx, stroke_width=10
        )
        dx_label = MathTex("dx", color=color_dx, font_size=30)
        dx_label.next_to(dx_segment, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(input_line), FadeIn(input_label))
        self.play(Create(dx_segment), FadeIn(dx_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_dy))
        
        dy_start_num = 3.0
        dy_length_initial = dx_val 
        dy_length_final = 1.5
        
        dy_segment = Line(
            output_line.number_to_point(dy_start_num),
            output_line.number_to_point(dy_start_num + dy_length_initial),
            color=color_dy, stroke_width=10
        )
        dy_label = MathTex("dy", color=color_dy, font_size=30)
        dy_label.next_to(dy_segment, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(output_line), FadeIn(output_label))
        self.play(Create(dy_segment), FadeIn(dy_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(color_formula))
        
        stretch_tracker = ValueTracker(dy_length_initial)
        
        dy_segment.add_updater(
            lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners([
                output_line.number_to_point(dy_start_num),
                output_line.number_to_point(dy_start_num + stretch_tracker.get_value())
            ])
        )
        dy_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dy_segment, DOWN, buff=0.1))
        
        formula = MathTex(
            "f'(x) = \\frac{dy}{dx} = \\frac{1.5}{0.5} = 3", 
            color=color_formula, font_size=36
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, "D1", "D6")
        
        self.play(
            stretch_tracker.animate.set_value(dy_length_final),
            Write(formula),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        dy_segment.clear_updaters()
        dy_label.clear_updaters()

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(color_text))
        
        highlight_box = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=color_formula, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(highlight_box))
        self.play(Indicate(dy_segment, color=color_dy, scale_factor=1.2))
        self.play(FadeOut(highlight_box))
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: The Direction of Transformation
outline.content: Explain the significance of the sign of the derivative in a transformational context. A positive derivative preserves the orientation (forward stays forward), while a negative derivative flips the space (forward becomes backward).
outline.example: If f(x) = -2x, the output line isn't just stretched; it's flipped horizontally. The ant walking right on the input line sees its shadow moving left on the output line.

A positive derivative preserves the original orientation of space.
A negative derivative flips the space in the output.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title_text = "The Direction of Transformation"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- The sign of the derivative determines the mapping's direction.",
            "- A positive derivative preserves the original orientation of space.",
            "- A negative derivative flips the space in the output."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_INPUT = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_POSITIVE = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_NEGATIVE = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The sign of the derivative determines the mapping's direction."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_INPUT)

        # Input and Output Lines
        # Using columns 3-6 for the lines to maintain gap from lecture text (B021)
        input_line = NumberLine(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], length=3.5, include_numbers=True, font_size=18, color=COLOR_INPUT)
        output_line = NumberLine(x_range=[-6, 6, 2], length=3.5, include_numbers=True, font_size=18, color=COLOR_INPUT)
        
        self.place_in_area(input_line, 'B3', 'B6')
        self.place_in_area(output_line, 'E3', 'E6')
        
        input_label = Text("Input", font_size=20, color=COLOR_INPUT)
        output_label = Text("Output", font_size=20, color=COLOR_INPUT)
        
        # Position labels offset from the movement area (B013)
        self.place_at_grid(input_label, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(output_label, 'E2', scale_factor=0.8)

        # Initial function display
        func_label = MathTex("f(x) = 2x", font_size=36, color=COLOR_POSITIVE)
        self.place_in_area(func_label, 'C3', 'C6')

        self.play(
            Create(input_line),
            Create(output_line),
            Write(input_label),
            Write(output_label),
            Write(func_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "A positive derivative preserves the original orientation of space."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_POSITIVE)

        # ValueTracker for smooth movement
        t = ValueTracker(0)

        # Create arrows that will be updated by the ValueTracker
        input_arrow = Arrow(color=COLOR_INPUT, stroke_width=4, buff=0)
        output_arrow = Arrow(color=COLOR_POSITIVE, stroke_width=4, buff=0)

        def update_input_arrow(mob):
            val = t.get_value()
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(input_line.n2p(val), input_line.n2p(val + 0.5))

        def update_output_arrow_pos(mob):
            val = t.get_value()
            # f(x) = 2x mapping
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(output_line.n2p(2 * val), output_line.n2p(2 * (val + 0.5)))

        input_arrow.add_updater(update_input_arrow)
        output_arrow.add_updater(update_output_arrow_pos)

        self.add(input_arrow, output_arrow)
        # Animate from 0 to 1 on the input line
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(1), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "A negative derivative flips the space in the output."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_NEGATIVE)

        # Transition to f(x) = -2x
        new_func_label = MathTex("f(x) = -2x", font_size=36, color=COLOR_NEGATIVE)
        self.place_in_area(new_func_label, 'C3', 'C6')

        # Reset ValueTracker and update the output arrow behavior
        self.play(
            FadeOut(input_arrow),
            FadeOut(output_arrow),
            Transform(func_label, new_func_label),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        t.set_value(0)
        output_arrow.remove_updater(update_output_arrow_pos)
        output_arrow.set_color(COLOR_NEGATIVE)

        def update_output_arrow_neg(mob):
            val = t.get_value()
            # f(x) = -2x mapping
            # Input forward: [val, val+0.5] -> Output: [-2*val, -2*(val+0.5)]
            # Since -2*(val+0.5) < -2*val, the arrow points left (reversal)
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(output_line.n2p(-2 * val), output_line.n2p(-2 * (val + 0.5)))

        # Highlight reversal of orientation with a brief flash (FF0000)
        flash = Flash(output_line.n2p(0), color=COLOR_NEGATIVE, flash_radius=0.5)
        
        self.play(flash)
        
        input_arrow.add_updater(update_input_arrow)
        output_arrow.add_updater(update_output_arrow_neg)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(input_arrow),
            FadeIn(output_arrow)
        )
        
        # Animate movement showing the flipped direction
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(1), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

        # Final cleanup
        input_arrow.remove_updater(update_input_arrow)
        output_arrow.remove_updater(update_output_arrow_neg)

outline.title: Density and Compression
outline.content: Introduce the concept of 'Point Density'. Where the derivative is high, points are spread out (dilated). Where the derivative is near zero, points are crowded together (compressed). This leads to the idea of critical points being 'singularities' where the transformation momentarily collapses space.
outline.example: At x=0 for f(x)=x³, the derivative is 0. This 'crushes' a whole neighborhood of input points into a single dense cluster on the output line before they start stretching out again.

storyboard.title: Density and Compression
lecture_lines: Derivatives also reveal how point density changes during mapping.
High derivatives spread points out, creating lower density.
Low derivatives crowd points together, increasing the local density.
At critical points, the derivative is zero, collapsing space.
This 'crushing' effect happens momentarily before space expands again.

        point_x = Dot(point=self.grid["B2"], color="#00FF00")
        label_x = MathTex("x", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        # Position label_x above the point (Grid A2) - Resolving Issue #27 and #28
        self.place_at_grid(label_x, "A2", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Draw an initial arrow showing mapping from Input 'x' (B2) to Output 'f(x)' (E4)
        # In f(x)=2x, the distance ratio is 2, mapping Col 2 to Col 4.
        mapping_arrow = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["B2"], 
            end=self.grid["E4"], 
            buff=0.1, 
            color="#00FFFF", 
            stroke_width=3
        )
        point_fx = Dot(point=self.grid["E4"], color="#00FFFF")
        label_fx = MathTex("f(x)", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        # Position label_fx below the point (Grid F4) - Resolving Issue #28
        self.place_at_grid(label_fx, "F4", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(FadeIn(point_x), Write(label_x))
        self.play(GrowArrow(mapping_arrow), FadeIn(point_fx), Write(label_fx))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # For f(x)=2x, every point moves twice as far. Show multiple arrows.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # Define points mapping x to 2x using distance from an origin at imaginary Col 0.
        # B1 (dist 1) -> E2 (dist 2)
        # B2 (dist 2) -> E4 (dist 4)
        # B3 (dist 3) -> E6 (dist 6)
        points_input = [self.grid["B1"], self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B3"]]
        points_output = [self.grid["E2"], self.grid["E4"], self.grid["E6"]]
        
        arrows = VGroup(*[
            Arrow(start=pi, end=po, buff=0.1, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2) 
            for pi, po in zip(points_input, points_output)
        ])
        
        # Remove the previous single arrow/dot to avoid duplication when showing the group
        self.remove(mapping_arrow, point_fx)
        
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in arrows], lag_ratio=0.3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)
